title: Spacing and Flex Utilities
summary: A Bootstrap utility class has one small job, such as adding space or making a row of boxes.
introduction: A Bootstrap utility class has one small job, such as adding space or making a row of boxes. Use padding for space inside a box and margin for space outside it. Then add a flex row with a small gap between its items.
learningObjectives: Read and write spacing classes using the property, side and size scheme
Lay out elements with the flex direction, alignment, wrapping and gap utilities
Apply display, sizing, position, colour, border and shadow utilities
Decide when a utility beats a custom CSS rule

blocks.text: Spacing classes follow one pattern: **property**, **side**, dash, **size**. The property is `m` for margin or `p` for padding. The side is `t` (top), `b` (bottom), `s` (start, the left in left-to-right pages), `e` (end), `x` (both horizontal), `y` (both vertical) or nothing for all four. The size is a step on a scale based on the `1rem` spacer. So `mt-3` is `margin-top: 1rem`, `px-2` is horizontal padding of `.5rem`, and `m-0` removes all margins. Insert a breakpoint before the size for a responsive version: `mt-md-5`.

blocks.text: `auto` is the one special size. `mx-auto` on a block element with a width centres it horizontally, the classic CSS trick with no CSS written. Negative margins (`mt-n3`) exist in the Sass source but are switched off in the compiled CDN build, so do not expect them to work unless you build Bootstrap yourself with `$enable-negative-margins: true`.

blocks.text: `d-flex` turns an element into a flex container; after that the utilities map almost one to one onto [CSS flexbox](/tutorials/css) properties. `flex-row` and `flex-column` set the direction, `justify-content-*` distributes items along it (`start`, `end`, `center`, `between`, `around`, `evenly`), `align-items-*` aligns them across it (`start`, `end`, `center`, `baseline`, `stretch`), `flex-wrap` allows wrapping, `flex-fill` makes items share the space equally, `order-*` reorders them and `gap-*` spaces them on the same scale as margins. Every one of these takes a breakpoint infix, which is how a column of boxes on a phone becomes a row on a tablet.

blocks.text: Inside a flex row, `me-auto` on an item pushes everything after it to the far end and `ms-auto` pushes the item itself to the end, which is how a navbar sends its search form to the right. Bootstrap also ships two helpers, `vstack` and `hstack`, which are `d-flex flex-column` and `d-flex flex-row align-items-center` with sensible defaults for stacking buttons or form controls.

`d-*` sets `display` (covered in the breakpoints lesson). Sizing utilities set percentages of the parent: `w-25`, `w-50`, `w-75`, `w-100`, `w-auto` and the same for `h-*`, plus `mw-100` and `mh-100` for max sizes and `vw-100`, `vh-100`, `min-vh-100` for the viewport. Position utilities set `position-{static|relative|absolute|fixed|sticky}` and the offsets `top-0`, `top-50`, `top-100`, `bottom-*`, `start-*`, `end-*`; `translate-middle` shifts an element back by half its size so those offsets refer to its centre. The classic sticky footer needs only three of them.

blocks.text: `bg-{colour}` and `text-{colour}` use the theme palette, and `text-bg-{colour}` sets both with a readable pairing. Bootstrap 5.3 adds `bg-{colour}-subtle` (a pale tint), `text-{colour}-emphasis` (a dark shade) and `border-{colour}-subtle`, which together make a tinted panel that still works in dark mode. Borders start with `border` and are adjusted with sides (`border-top`), widths (`border-2`) and colours; corners with `rounded`, `rounded-0` to `rounded-5`, `rounded-circle` and `rounded-pill`; depth with `shadow-sm`, `shadow` and `shadow-lg`.

blocks.title: Common mistake: Bootstrap 4 side letters
blocks.text: `ml-2`, `mr-3`, `pl-0` and `float-left` are Bootstrap 4 names. Version 5 renamed left and right to **start** and **end** so that layouts flip correctly in right-to-left languages: `ms-2`, `me-3`, `ps-0`, `float-start`, `text-start`. The old classes are not defined in the 5.3 stylesheet, so they do nothing and produce no error; a margin that "does not work" is usually one of these.

items: Use a utility when the adjustment is local and visible in the markup: spacing, alignment, a border, a colour from the palette.
Write CSS when the same combination appears on many elements (give it a class name) or when the value is not on Bootstrap's scales (a 37px gap, a brand colour that is not in the theme).
Utilities carry `!important`, so they override component and custom styles. If a utility refuses to apply, something is overriding it with `!important` too, or the class name is misspelled.
Prefer colour-mode-aware classes (`bg-body-tertiary`, `text-body-secondary`, `border`) over fixed ones (`bg-light`, `text-dark`, `bg-white`) so the page survives a switch to dark mode.

blocks.title: Read a class, predict the CSS
blocks.text: Before adding a class, say its CSS aloud: `py-md-4` is "padding top and bottom of 1.5rem from the md breakpoint". If you cannot translate a class into a property and value, look it up before using it.

questions.question: What CSS does `py-3` apply?
questions.explanation: p is padding, y is both vertical sides, and size 3 is 1rem on the spacing scale.

questions.question: Inside a `d-flex` row, `me-auto` on the first item pushes all the following items to the far end.
questions.explanation: An auto margin in a flex container absorbs the free space, so margin-end: auto on the first item leaves the rest at the end of the row.
